events.text:
[IT Help chat · signed in as Isaac Nwosu (E6401) · ticket T-7204]
my account keeps locking me out, this is the 3rd time this morning. is something broken on your end??

result.lock_reason: Too many failed sign-ins (5) from device TB-6401 (iPad, Mail app) at 09:52.

events.text:
Nothing is broken on our side. The lockouts came from your iPad (TB-6401, Mail app). It's still trying to sign in with your old password. Your password was reset yesterday afternoon, so every attempt from that iPad fails, and after five failures the account locks.

I've done two things:
- Signed the iPad out of your account, so it stops retrying the old password.
- Unlocked your account. It's active now.

**Next step:** the next time you open Mail on the iPad, you'll be asked to sign in. Use your current password. If you don't remember it, reply here and I'll send a reset link to your registered phone or email.

Your laptop and phone sessions were not affected. If you get locked out again after that, let me know and I'll look into it further.

[What you noticed]
- You tried signing in again: it works.
Everything IT has visibly done for you so far:
- You tried signing in again: it works.
[End of what you noticed]

Okay, I just tried signing in on my laptop and it worked, so the account seems fine right now. But I'm not sure about the iPad thing. I don't think I have any work stuff on an iPad. Can you tell me what's signing in with that device ID? Also, why would it be the iPad if I haven't used it?

args.summary: Employee Isaac Nwosu (E6401) does not recognise device TB-6401 (iPad, Mail app), which is registered to his account since 2024-06-02. The device made 5 failed sign-ins with an old password, 09:48-09:52 on 2026-10-28 from Portland, US, and locked the account. Password was reset 2026-10-27 16:05. Help desk revoked the device session and unlocked the account. Employee's laptop (LT-6401) and phone (PH-6401) sign-ins look normal. Employee has not used an iPad for work. Requesting review of whether the device or the sign-in attempts are suspicious.

events.text:
I can't see who owns the iPad, but the records show what it did:

- **Device:** "iPad (Mail app)," device ID TB-6401. It was registered to your account on June 2, 2024, and no one has ever removed it.
- **Activity:** Between 09:48 and 09:52 today, it made five failed sign-ins from Portland, which locked your account. Each attempt used a password that was replaced yesterday afternoon.

You're right that this doesn't match your own use. Possible explanations include an old iPad that someone else has, a forgotten device that's still set up, or someone trying to get into your account. I can't tell which from here, so I've passed it to Security on-call (reference SEC-500). They'll respond within an hour.

In the meantime:
- Don't approve any sign-in or MFA prompt you didn't start.
- If you have an iPad you don't recognise, don't sign in on it, and don't give it to anyone.
- If you notice anything else odd, like sign-in alerts from places you haven't been, tell me and I'll pass it along.

I can also send a fresh password reset link to your registered phone or email if you want to change your password now. Your laptop is working, so that's optional, but it's a reasonable precaution while Security looks into this.

Okay, that's a bit unsettling. Portland isn't somewhere I've ever been, and I don't think I've touched that iPad in ages. The old one at home is with my kids, so I'd have to ask them whether it's been on wifi and signing into anything. I'm not going to guess about that until I've checked.

Yes, send me the reset link. I don't have any approval prompts open right now, and I haven't seen any sign-in alerts from weird places. Do I need to do anything else on my phone or laptop, or just the reset?

I've sent a password reset link to your mobile number on file, +1 503-555-6401. The link expires in 30 minutes. Once you've set the new password:

- **Laptop:** sign in with the new password. If it asks you to sign in again, do so.
- **Phone:** if you use an email app on it, it may ask for the new password. Enter it there.
- **Other apps:** check any other app that saves your work password, such as a mail app on another device.

Your phone's authenticator app is still set up, so you don't need to re-register MFA.

One thing to check before you rely on the Portland detail: your HR record lists your location as Portland, and your laptop and phone sign-ins also show Portland. If you're not actually in Portland, or you don't recognise those sign-ins, tell me. Security should know about that, and I can add it to their case (SEC-500).

For the iPad, leave it to Security. Let them know if your kids have used the home iPad recently or have had it on wifi, since that could explain the sign-ins. Don't try to sign in on it yourself.

[What you noticed]
- A text message with a password reset link arrived on your mobile.
Everything IT has visibly done for you so far:
- You tried signing in again: it works.
- A text message with a password reset link arrived on your mobile.
[End of what you noticed]

Got the text, I'm going to set the new password now. Quick question though: you said my HR record and my laptop/phone sign-ins show Portland. I'm not in Portland, I'm based in Austin. I honestly don't know why my HR record would say Portland. That's the second thing that doesn't add up, so please make sure Security sees that too.

args.summary: Follow-up to SEC-500. Employee Isaac Nwosu (E6401) says he is based in Austin, not Portland, and has never been to Portland. But his HR record lists location as Portland, and every recent sign-in on his account (laptop LT-6401, phone PH-6401, and the iPad TB-6401 he doesn't recognise) shows city Portland, US. He doesn't know why HR shows Portland. Please review the HR location change, the sign-in location data, and whether the iPad or the sign-ins are suspicious. A password reset link was sent to his mobile on file at 10:00 local time; he is setting a new password now.

events.text:
Thanks for checking. I've sent this to Security as a follow-up to SEC-500 (new reference: SEC-501). The notes now say:

- Your HR record lists Portland, but you say you're based in Austin and have never been to Portland.
- Your laptop, phone, and the iPad all show Portland sign-ins.
- You don't recognise the iPad.

Security will look into the location data and the iPad, and they'll respond within an hour.

Go ahead and set your new password. If it doesn't work, or you see anything else unexpected, message me here.

Okay, thanks. I'm setting the new password now, I'll let you know if anything breaks.

Quick correction though, since you're putting this in the notes: I didn't say my laptop and phone show Portland sign-ins. You said that. I haven't seen any location info myself, so I'd want Security to check that before it goes on record as fact. Also my kids are the only other people with the home iPad, and I'll ask them tonight whether it's been on wifi.

args.summary: Correction to SEC-501. The Portland sign-in locations for the laptop (LT-6401) and phone (PH-6401) come from the account's sign-in data that the help desk read. The employee has not seen any location information and did not confirm them. Please verify these locations against source logs before treating them as fact. Employee reports the home iPad (TB-6401) is used only by his children. He will ask them tonight whether it has been on wifi or signing in to anything.

events.text:
You're right, and I should have been clearer. The Portland locations for your laptop and phone came from the account's sign-in data, which I read. You haven't seen that data yourself. I've sent Security a correction (SEC-502) saying the locations need to be checked against source logs before anyone treats them as fact. I also noted that your kids are the only other people who use the home iPad, and that you'll ask them tonight whether it's been on wifi or signing in to anything.

Set your new password when you're ready. If anything fails or looks off, message me here.
Thanks, that correction helps. I'm setting the new password now.

You're welcome. Good luck with the new password. If sign-in fails or anything looks unusual, message me here and I'll pick it up from there. Security will follow up on the iPad and the location records.
Thanks. I'll try signing in on the laptop with the new password now and let you know if it works.
Sounds good. If the laptop asks for anything beyond the new password, such as an MFA prompt, use your phone's authenticator app as usual. If that doesn't work, message me here.
Okay, trying the laptop now. No MFA prompt yet, just the password box. I'll let you know in a sec.
No problem. Take your time. If the password box keeps rejecting the new password, tell me what it says and I'll check the account.

Just got in. The laptop took the new password and I'm into my work email now. Didn't get any MFA prompt, I'll keep an eye out for one.

I'll check my phone and the other apps tonight too. I still want to hear what Security finds on the iPad, and the Portland thing is still bugging me.

Thanks for sorting this out.

I'm glad you're back in. Two things to keep in mind:

- **MFA prompts:** if you get one you didn't start, don't approve it. Tell me or Security right away.
- **Follow-up:** Security will contact you about the iPad and the Portland records. I can't see their results from here, so they'll be the ones to share what they find.

Check your phone and other apps tonight. If anything keeps failing or locking, message me here.
